title: Harborcrest - renewal & expansion provisioning check-in
text:
Harborcrest - renewal & expansion provisioning check-in

summary:
Quarterly renewal/check-in to confirm renewal timing, scope for capacity uplift, APAC + EU region onboarding timeline, and to run through security docs and a short benchmark plan. Customer is leaning toward a Dedicated + VPC private pilot for EU, wants clearer latency SLOs and KMS integration notes. Agreed next steps: SE to share benchmark sheet and perf targets, AE to send updated pricing and renewal amendment draft, customer to provide expected QPS profile and timeline.

topics:
Renewal timing and contract extension options
Capacity uplift (monthly tokens / steady throughput / burst)
APAC + EU region provisioning and private VPC pilot
Security (SOC 2, KMS/HSM, audit logs) and egress costs
Benchmark plan and SLA/latency targets

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-03-27 14:30 PDT / Duration: ~46m / Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Michael, Dana, Klaus (Harborcrest)

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jared with Redwood, I'm the AE on your account, and Priya here is our SE. Quick check — audio okay?
[00:07] Michael: Yep, good here. Thanks Jared.
[00:09] Priya: Hi all, Priya — will run the perf bits later, but first wanted to confirm objectives for today.
[00:15] Dana: We're aiming to lock renewal terms and confirm region onboard windows — EU private pilot for compliance and APAC for latency, basically.
[00:23] Jared: Great, so agenda — renewal timing and amendments, capacity bump sizing, provisioning timeline for EU VPC and APAC edge, and then security + benchmarks.
[00:30] Klaus: That's right. We also want KMS integration notes; legal wants a sense of audit logging and retention.
[00:36] Priya: Perfect — on the KMS front we support customer-managed keys via most cloud KMS providers and can integrate with HSMs for private. There's an ops playbook we can share, I will post link after.
[00:46] Michael: Quick question — are there any differences in latency between Dedicated and Private in EU? We care about tail latency for inference.
[00:53] Priya: Short answer: not inherently, it depends on instance types and network topology. Dedicated (hosted dedicated pool) gives predictable throughput and we've tuned the runtime kernels; Private (VPC) adds a bit of network overhead depending on peering and egress. In our tests we saw median latency parity, but p95-ish can vary 10-30ms if there's cross-region routing.
[01:12] Dana: Hm, 10-30ms p95 variation is significant for us. Our SLAs are tight. Can we do a baseline run from our EU region to confirm?
[01:20] Priya: Absolutely — that's the benchmark plan we'll run. I'll need an IP whitelist + small test corpus and sample QPS.
[01:26] Jared: We'll draft an test-run checklist. Also pricing note — if you commit to dedicated capacity across EU+APAC we can offer a term amendment with reduced unit rates; I'll send numbers.
[01:38] Klaus: What's the minimum commit you're expecting? Last time we talked there was a three-month ramp.
[01:42] Jared: We're flexible. For a Dedicated pool for your forecasted peak we recommend committing to a 6-month window for the best pricing, but there's a monthly cadence option. We'll outline both in the amendment.
[01:51] Michael: On capacity numbers — our initial ask is to double active tokens from current baseline. Right now our steady QPS is about 120 rps, bursts to 420 during lead times. We need to bump throughput and preserve low tail latency.
[02:03] Priya: That helps. We'll model continuous batching and KV prefix cache behavior — if you provide token distributions (prompt sizes + average generated tokens), we can give a recommended pooling config and estimated GPU slot counts.
[02:14] Dana: We'll send token distribution by EOD tomorrow. Is there an upper bound on burst capacity? We need some headroom for holiday spikes.
[02:21] Jared: We offer burst capacity for dedicated; it's not unlimited but we can provision buffer headroom. Pricing differs for burst usage vs committed.
[02:27] Klaus: And disaster fallback — if dedicated pool in EU is saturated, can traffic fail over to hosted fallback in another region? We need graceful degradation.
[02:35] Priya: Yes, smart routing policies allow that — can route by cost or latency and fallback to a compatible model in another region. You'll configure that in rollout policy. There is a slight latency impact but better than failing.
[02:47] Michael: Good. On the private pilot — timeline? We prefer EU private pilot before signing full extension.
[02:52] Jared: Reasonable. Proposed timeline: week 1 — contract amendment and SOW; week 2-3 — VPC peering and KMS setup; week 4 — provisioning and smoke tests; week 5 — performance benchmarks and readout. We can compress some steps if your infra team is ready.
[03:08] Dana: Does Redwood manage the control plane in private or is it customer-managed?
[03:12] Priya: For Private we run a customer-managed control plane option or a hybrid control plane depending on compliance needs. For most EU pilots we keep the control plane minimal and provide an ops runbook.
[03:21] Klaus: Ok legal will want the details on data flows. Can you share the data residency sheet?
[03:25] Jared: Yes, will attach SOC2 + residency doc in the follow-up.
[03:29] Michael: On encryption — will audit logs be accessible via our SIEM?
[03:33] Priya: We can stream audit logs to your cloud logging endpoint; we also support S3 pull for long-term retention. Egress costs will apply.
[03:40] Dana: Please include estimated egress for our projected QPS in the next quote.
[03:44] Jared: Noted.
[03:45] [03:45] Jared: Priya, could you walk through the benchmark steps quickly?
[03:48] Priya: Sure — we'll run three phases: cold-start latency and tails, steady-state throughput with batching, and KV/prefix cache hit-rate sensitivity. We'll also test quantized model variants to check cost vs quality. For EU private pilot we'll focus on p95/p99 for 512-token context, plus a 2k sequence run for some heavy prompts.
[04:08] Michael: Quantized variants okay, but any quality regression concerns? We need to map quality drop vs cost.
[04:13] Priya: We'll include a small eval set of your prompts to compute quality deltas and give recommendations; that's part of Redwood Optimize suggestions.
[04:20] Klaus: Will Redwood provide a performance SLA for p99 or p95? Our procurement pushes for p99 < 500ms for edge requests.
[04:28] Jared: We provide latency targets by tier; p95 is typically guaranteed within the SLA for Dedicated — p99 is trickier; we can include fallback and mitigation clauses. We'll surface exact numbers in the amendment.
[04:40] Dana: On the security review — are there any outstanding gaps from our earlier security questionnaire? We sent in a few clarifying questions last month.
[04:47] Priya: Most were addressed; remaining items were around key rotation and HSM attestation— we can provide HKMS/HSM integration notes and rotation cadence. I'll attach our KMS runbook.
[04:56] Michael: Also, can you confirm retention windows for logs? We need 7 years for certain events.
[05:01] Priya: We support configurable retention; for 7 years we'll need an archival path (S3) and that will be part of the compliance add-on.
[05:09] Klaus: Any vendor competitors we should beware of? Our security team mentioned another provider that does on-prem appliances.
[05:15] Jared: We did hear you mention Anthropic earlier in due diligence; other customers evaluate self-hosted appliance vendors. We'll include a short comparison doc.
[05:24] Michael: Helpful. Ok, next — can we walk through the immediate next steps?
[05:28] Jared: Yes. Proposed next steps: Priya shares benchmark spreadsheet + ops runbook; Jared sends renewal amendment + pricing options (6-month commit vs monthly); Harborcrest shares token distribution and IPs for whitelist; schedule kickoff for private pilot next Tuesday if everyone's available.
[05:44] Dana: Tuesday works tentatively. I'll confirm after internal sync.
[05:47] Michael: We'll send token distribution today.
[05:49] Priya: Quick note — for the private EU pilot we'll need a handful of service accounts and one engineer with access to set up peering. Ideally, provide access window mid-day UTC.
[06:00] Klaus: We'll allocate resources.
[06:02] Jared: Any remaining blockers?
[06:04] Dana: Only legal's final wording on data flows — otherwise good.
[06:08] Michael: No other blockers. Thanks everyone.
[06:10] Jared: Great — we'll follow up with docs and a draft amendment by EOD tomorrow. Thanks for your time.

End of meeting.


action_items:
Priya Nand: Share benchmark spreadsheet + KMS runbook (due 2025-04-02)
Jared Kim: Send renewal amendment draft with 6-month and monthly commit pricing options (due 2025-03-28)
Michael O'Leary: Provide token distribution, prompt size & QPS profile (due 2025-03-27 EOD)
Dana Ruiz: Confirm private pilot kickoff availability and provide engineer contact for peering (due 2025-03-28)
Redwood Ops: Attach SOC2 + data residency document in follow-up (owner: Jared)

next_steps:
Send security and residency docs
Share benchmark plan and schedule pilot run
Provide pricing amendment and egress estimate
Schedule private pilot kickoff (tentative next Tuesday)
